Technical report · measurement · sweep of 2026-08-10

The vacuous green — passing and being checked are independent properties

A green check certifies that what it evaluated was acceptable. It is silent about how much it evaluated — and those are different properties, independently variable, of which only the first is ever asserted. Measured three times with three instruments at three layers of one codebase and one public benchmark: the checks that guard builds, the suites that grade benchmark solutions, and the batteries that validate numerics. The same shape appears at every layer, it survives perfect scores on mutation testing — the strongest widely-used adequacy measure — and the instruments built to detect it have themselves committed it.

1 · The scar that motivates the question

The Erdős #290 constant was wrong from the sixth decimal, live on the public site and in an OEIS draft, under all gates green — the kernel's own check asserted a bracket that both the wrong and the right value satisfy.

Three of the five checks in the adversarial pass had 'confirmed' the wrong constant — they verified transcription fidelity, not truth. The catch came from an adversarial pass whose brief was to re-derive every number by a deliberately different method — not from any gate. The lesson that survives is the question this page asks of every check: what value would this reject? A check that cannot fail for any value the defect could produce is a comment with a green tick beside it. This report asks the quantitative version: how much of its subject can a check lose before its silence becomes the defect?

2 · The field named this by 2001

A check that reports success having evaluated nothing passes vacuously. A precise verdict over too little input has a name in the literature, and the name is not ours. The term is the title: Beer, Ben-David, Eisner & Rodeh, 'Efficient Detection of Vacuity in Temporal Model Checking', Formal Methods in System Design 18(2):141–163, 2001 — a 1997 predecessor title exists, and which paper is the first naming is left open here. A later refinement carries the adjacent term in its title: Ben-David, Fisman & Ruah, 'Temporal Antecedent Failure: Refining Vacuity', CONCUR 2007, LNCS 4703, pp. 492–506. Both cited from fetched bibliographic records; neither body has been reached, and nothing here characterises their content. What is claimed on this page is the measurement where the antecedent is a directory listing, not the phenomenon. (doi:10.1023/A:1008779610539 · doi:10.1007/978-3-540-74407-8_33.)

Vacuity detection lives in temporal model checking, where the antecedent is a formula. In the passes run so far, no work was found applying it to the checks measured below — a search result, not a property of the literature; the primary-text pass that could settle it is recorded as owed. What is measured here are checks whose antecedent is a directory listing — a build gate sweeping a tree, a benchmark item running its suite, a battery walking its goldens. There, the vacuous pass has a specific shape: the sweep comes up short and the verdict does not move.

3 · Layer one: build gates, and the perturbation that matters

A red control proves a check notices a wrong value. Whether it notices missing work is a separate property, and the two perturbations separate cleanly:

Deleting a slice of what a check reads: 12 of 12 gates noticed. Narrowing the sweep with the tree untouched: 4 of 8 stayed green. Deletion measures "does it assert its subjects exist," which nearly everything does. Narrowing — the tree intact, the walk returning less — is the honest simulation of a walk gone quiet, and it is the one that found blindness. Concretely, on 2026-08-09: check-narration read 106 of 599 (lost 82%), check-ships 9 of 37 (76%), check-cert-pins 5 of 21 (76%), check-ip 3 of 4 (25%) — all still green. On 2026-08-09, narrowed to 5 of the 21 record files it should have read, check-cert-pins stayed green and printed: cert pins green — every byte every cert names is the byte on disk. (A dated record of the narrowed run: the gate counts pins, the sweep counts files read, and the gate's own totals have since changed.)

The full 47-target sweep found six gates blind (check-ships, check-cert-pins, check-narration, check-ip, check-ledger, check-lab-export); all six were repaired and the rate read 0 of 10 after. One day after the six repairs, the sweep found check-ledger blind again at a 34% shrink — and the committed record was left standing while the present-tense document was corrected.

Today's full sweep, from the raw log committed beside this page (domain-collapse-all-2026-08-10.log):

The blind gate today is check-ledger, green after losing 34% of what it reads — one of the six repaired the day before. The narrowing is deterministic by index — a target narrows the same way twice — so the committed log is the run, and agreement between re-runs is expected rather than evidential. Whether the gate regressed or was never sufficient at that shrink is not established; the run measures the symptom. What is established is the pattern: this class of defect comes back, and a one-time cleanup does not hold.

The 37 targets whose domain never shrank are reported as not applicable, not as passes — and not applicable is a statement about the instrument's reach, not a clearance. Most read declared lists, where there is nothing to collapse; some enumerate by means the tracer's readdirSync hook cannot shrink (git listings, computed sets), and those are unmeasured — the bucket may contain blind gates the instrument cannot see. The blind rate above is a rate among the 10 the instrument could measure. Folding the rest into green would have manufactured a reassuring denominator, which is this page's own subject.

4 · Layer two: a public benchmark's own suites

The same question, asked of HumanEval: if the solution were wrong, would this item's own tests notice? Two independent probes, both published with their batteries at evidence-first-bench and verifier-audit:

  • Mechanical. Mutating each reference solution and running the item's own suite: 759/853 mutants killed (rate 0.8898), and 3 of 154 in-scope items (1.9%) cannot distinguish the reference from a deliberately broken copy at all. 10 items are out of scope for mutation and excluded from that denominator — named here because a dropped population is this page's own subject.
  • Realistic. Against plausible wrong solutions, each proven wrong by an independent witness input: 24 of 163 items — 14.7% — accept the wrong solution. 18 of the 24 had been rated sensitive by mutation, and 10 of them carry a mutation kill rate of exactly 1.00 — recomputed for this page by joining the two result files, not quoted.
A perfect mutation score is not sufficient evidence that a test suite is sound. Conditioning on a perfect score lowers the false-pass rate — 14.7% overall against 9.7% among the 103 perfect scorers — so it is evidence; it is nowhere near clearance: 10 of those 103 verifiers fail against a plausible wrong solution (95% CI [5.4, 17]), and the score-to-soundness correlation is -0.1658 over n=153 — weak, marginally significant at best, and no basis for trusting any individual suite.

The three layers share a shape, not a mechanism. A benchmark item's suite is a check whose domain is the behaviour space of the problem, and a suite of two assertions has narrowed that domain to two points — but that is a specification deficiency no directory walk produced, measured by a different instrument. What is claimed across the layers is the shape and its consequence — a PASS over two points is reported with the same green as a PASS over the space, and no score column says how much was looked at — not an identity of cause.

5 · Layer three: the batteries that validate numerics

The tree these gates guard honours the rule that a skip is never a pass — every guarded absence prints a red row. The size of what the row hides is another matter: Before the 2026-08-09 repair: 19 assertion-guarding skips hiding 57 assertions, p90 = 6 per guard, 5 with no report at all, and 0 of 19 telling the reader the size. The instance that paid for the measurement: Seven assertions sat dark behind one red row in a mare-farm battery — a 27-row battery reporting 21 rows and calling itself whole.

The repair that held was the one that writes no number down: delete the guard, let every comparison fail on its own, and the battery's row total no longer moves — measured by hiding each subject and restoring it across six batteries. A hole can no longer disguise itself as a smaller battery — enforced by arithmetic a reader does in their head, not by a sentence someone maintains. And the repair demonstrated the trap once more on its way in: The repair itself minted one more vacuous pass before it was caught: with the guard deleted, JSON.stringify(undefined) === JSON.stringify(undefined) compared quietly green on a missing golden.

Residual state, measured for this page: 7 assertion-guarding skips hiding 40 assertions (p90 13), 0 silent, 22 batteries printing sized skips. The split remains clean — a battery sizes every skip or sizes none.

6 · The third direction: a red that proves nothing

While this page was being assembled, its own ritual produced the mirror image. The checking layer is wrong in a third direction too: a pre-push ritual printed a false RED manufactured by its own concurrency — one gate's red control mutating shared state while a neighbour read it. Reproduced 4 of 5 staggered runs, then made hermetic and proven both directions.

The symmetry completes the claim. A checking layer can be wrong three ways: green over unexamined work (vacuous pass), red over nothing (a race, a crash read as a verdict), and right for the wrong reason (transcription agreement). Only the middle one is loud, and even it is loud in a way that erodes trust in red — every false red teaches a reader that red sometimes means nothing. The instruments below exist because none of the three is visible from inside a summary line.

7 · The instruments catch their authors

Both measuring instruments in this report have, at least once, committed the defect they measure, and the audit path around them has once more:

  • The sweep's probe: The probe committed the defect it was built to find, on its first run — reporting '35 of 47 assert their denominator', a numerator whose own denominator was never checked.
  • The skip detector: its first version reported sizes wrong because it could not distinguish "absent" from "not looked for" — the same confusion one level up, recorded in the findings rather than quietly fixed.
  • The audit path beside them: A claim was written on a crashed search whose wrapper printed a hard-coded '(none found)' — a reassurance that could not tell a clean result from a dead one. The re-run found the answer was not zero.

And one honest negative, because the pattern invites over-claiming: The one eval harness available was tested for the same defect and pointed AWAY from the claim: the shape was latent, not live — 164 candidates, 164 problems, 0 dropped, and the harness was already careful. One harness is not a survey; it is the evidence to hand, and it is reported in the direction it points.

8 · The gate on this page, and what it could not see

The instruments listed above are the ones this report built. The check that guards this report belongs on the same list. A hostile read of the rendered page on 2026-08-10, the day it was built, returned 13 defects and 7 risks, with 5 further objections dropped by the reviewer for lack of evidence, and 1 advisory routed for IP review. That advisory was the one objection about a gate's own reach — that the narration gate did not scan gated pages — and on 2026-08-21 it was tested rather than assumed: a private path planted in a gated page turns that gate red, and removing it turns it green. The gate does scan them. The advisory is discharged, and it is named here rather than dropped from the tally, because a section about what a check could not see is the wrong place to quietly lose the one objection about what a check could not see. Each objection has a disposition in a committed record beside the builder; what earns a section here is not the tally but what the check on this page was doing while the referee worked.

The unit's own battery was green while blind to eight of the thirteen defects: its domain is the numbers that flow from the two data files into the page, and the defects lived in prose constants inside the builder, which a byte-identical rebuild reproduces perfectly. The battery enforces two couplings and enforces them well: the committed page must be byte-identical to a fresh build, and every dated number must still be present, verbatim, in the record it is pinned to. Neither coupling has an opinion about a sentence. A wrong number typed into a template string is regenerated faithfully on every run, and the byte comparison that proves the page was not hand-edited proves just as firmly that the wrong sentence was not hand-edited either. Green, and blind, for the reason the rest of this page argues.

Three of those eight were converted from prose constants into derived values — which gate is one of the six repaired, the battery denominator, the percentages in the sweep table. The rest are prose whose correctness no battery of this design can reach: the honest limit of a page that is generated rather than transcribed. Naming the remainder is the point. The two couplings are worth having and the tree keeps them; they are simply not the property a reader is looking for when a battery prints green. Their domain stops at the boundary between a number and a claim about a number. A green run here has always meant that this page is faithfully generated. It has never meant that this page is right.

9 · The anchor, still open

The case that motivated the instrument is still open: test-single-source.js prints its scanned-file count and asserts it zero times. It printed 'scanned 18' for an entire rebuild; the count moves, the silence does not. It stays open here by choice: closing the list would read better and would be the flattering omission this page exists to name. The count on screen today is asserted by nothing, and any reader can check whether that is still true faster than any summary of ours can go stale.

Scope, stated

Not claimed: the phenomenon (vacuity is named and tooled since 2001); any statement about benchmarks other than HumanEval; any statement that scoring harnesses in general carry the defect (the one tested did not — see §7); a fixed blind-rate for this tree (the applicable set is randomised: The early 8-target sample that read 50% blind was biased toward walking gates; the full-sweep figures are the honest ones. The applicable set varies between runs as the tree and each gate's domain change — a sample, not a fixed denominator; the narrowing itself is deterministic by index.).

Claimed, and falsifiable: that pass/checked independence is measurable wherever a check's antecedent is a listing, by one perturbation — narrow the input, re-run, watch the verdict; that on HumanEval mutation testing — the strongest widely-used adequacy measure — does not predict specification adequacy (10 perfect scores among 24 false-passes); and that in this tree the defect recurs after repair, so the instrument, not the fix, is the deliverable. Every claim names the command that re-measures it — today those commands run in this repository: the benchmark layers' programs are public at technical-reports/evidence-first-bench, and the export decision for this unit's own programs is recorded as owed before any promotion.

Carlos Toledo builds computer-assisted proofs and the checks that keep them honest. This page is the second half of the practice: a green result proves nothing until the check behind it has been shown to notice both a wrong value and a shrunken domain. The page carries its instruments' own failures beside their findings.
